farm.house: Press “Choose a house”, then set people to “Work on the house”: they fell the logs it needs and raise it. Until it stands, the family camps.
farm.field: Press “Plant the field” or tap a bare plot on the map: corn feeds the family and cotton sells. Planting uses seed, and the crop takes time to ripen.
farm.town: “Go to town to trade” sends someone to the store to buy and sell. They are away from the farm for the trip, and coin spent is gone from your score.

call.text: Your settlement is calling for men: press the “!”, tick who goes and press “Send them”. Each takes the rifle and powder, and with no answer in about 5 minutes the call closes.

sick.text: Someone is sick, and resting helps them mend. Have another grown-up press “Nurse the sick”: nobody dies while nursed, but a very sick person can die within a day.

tip.text: Your family is told to leave: press the “!”, load the wagon and press “Leave for the east”, or stay. No answer in time, and it leaves in a rush and the house is lost.

flight.label: The family has been told to leave for the east. No answer in time, and the family leaves in a rush — the house is lost, burned behind it. About 3 min left. Go to Hollis Proofwright and answer.

route.text: On the road east, the road is quicker but soldiers see you from farther off, and across country is slower and harder to see. “Change where we go” changes it.

tip.text: Soldiers shout “¡Alto!”, which means “Halt!”. Press the “!” and answer fast: halting loses the wagon and goods, running risks their shots, and no answer means you halt.

words: Soldiers shout “¡Alto!”, which means “Halt!”. Press the “!” and answer fast: halting loses the wagon and goods, running risks their shots, and no answer means you halt.
Press “Choose a house”, then set people to “Work on the house”: they fell the logs it needs and raise it. Until it stands, the family camps.
Tap one of your family on the left, then tap a job along the bottom; “More” shows the rest. A faded face with a ringed mark has nothing to do.
On the road east, the road is quicker but soldiers see you from farther off, and across country is slower and harder to see. “Change where we go” changes it.
“Stop and rest a day”: the sick mend twice as fast, but the family makes no miles and the Mexican army keeps coming.
The road is asking your family something. Press the “!” to answer: each answer says what it costs, and with no answer in time nothing is done.
Your family is told to leave: press the “!”, load the wagon and press “Leave for the east”, or stay. No answer in time, and it leaves in a rush and the house is lost.
A grown man can enlist, join a fight or go to vote from the jobs along the bottom. He is gone, with the family’s rifle, until you press “Send for them to come home”.
